title: Map the f(7) records; a second engine closes all 11 length-22 splits (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Navigation index plus a partial finite replay; no new bound, no κ, no supplier or frontier change. Card `scope-navigation` (consolidation), base `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`, priority revision 8. New package `research/f7-record-map`; no other file changes.

**Question.** Item 5 of petalas's [consolidation handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19230473) says the records disagree on f(7). #3058 says f(7) = 24, and `research/f7-independent-full-replay` (#3333) says `{22,24}`.

**Answer: they agree.** #3333 is a length-20 replay. It says it "does not decide whether length 22 is attainable". Length 22 is excluded on main by two routes that share no search code:

- #3058's covering-code argument, audited piecewise by #3224, #3244, #3261, #3276, #3287, #3360 and #3728.
- The census chain #2973 → #3708/#3712 → #3731/#3818 → #4221, bound to its domain by #4871.

The README's record map lists, for each length step, the route, the records, the independent coverage and what is still open. Every one of those records is `partially_reviewed` in the ledger.

**Second engine at length 22.** #4221's first open question, which #4871 repeats, is that every census-route L = 22 exclusion rests on one engine. The recorded blocker was that #3005's separately written engine "is gated at `L <= 20` and its throughput at length 22 is unmeasured". The gate is one constant. `verify.py` rebuilds #3005's `census.cpp` from the pinned bytes with exactly two lines changed (`max_length` and its error message) and runs it at n = 7, L = 22:

| Split | Entered nodes (this engine) | Hits | Prior engine nodes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `(11,9)` | 11,942,611,230 | 0 | #4221 14,058,107,415 |
| `(10,9)` | 6,624,261,154 | 0 | #4221 7,027,617,655 |
| `(11,8)` | 973,631,241 | 0 | #3731 1,349,702,650 |
| `(9,9)` | 386,427,869 | 0 | #3818 388,563,293 |
| `(10,8)` | 238,010,457 | 0 | #3731 597,933,297 |
| `(11,7)` | 8,613,944 | 0 | #3731 8,784,744 |
| `(10,7)` | 699,412 | 0 | #4221 700,909 |
| `(11,6)` | 1,020 | 0 | #4221 2,247 |
| `(11,11)` | 37,567,052,539 | 0 | #4221 55,385,607,437 |
| `(11,10)` | 40,743,043,536 | 0 | #4221 52,957,641,635 |
| `(10,10)` | 37,400,857,165 | 0 | #4221 44,378,511,529 |

**All 11 splits close on the second engine with zero hits**, all complete and uncapped. The three heaviest took 3,751 to 4,188 s each and were added in a follow-up commit. Every census-route L = 22 exclusion now rests on two separately written engines. The two engines are separately written, but #3818's engine ports #3005's union-support bound. The proof of that bound is therefore a premise of both; the code is not shared.

Controls:

- At L = 18 and L = 20, every summary field equals #3005's `FULL.json`.
- A capped n = 6, L = 22 run finds hits, and each one is checked by direct XOR coverage.
- A capped n = 7 run exits 2.
- Four tamper controls are rejected: a changed quote, a changed node count, a dropped domain split and a changed engine digest.

Entered-node counts track #3731/#3818: `(9,9)` gives 386,427,869 here against 388,563,293.

## Scope and limits

- The census route still imports #3708's four split conditions and its rotation symmetry, so only `s >= t` runs. It also relies on the pruning proofs of #3005 (this engine) and #3818 (the other engine).
- #3058 §3, the 21-distinct-prefix case, has no independent audit that I found on main. #3360 lists it as out of scope. Pattern A and 73 of the 77 pattern-B cases rest on the native search only.
- Consumers (#5234, #5430, #6005) cite only #3058. They use only the value, so the census route serves as well.
- The L = 22 runs are LOCAL-ONLY receipts (macOS arm64, Apple clang 21). CI replays `(11,6)`, `(10,7)` and `(11,7)` by default, and `(9,9)` and `(10,8)` in a second registered command.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-record-map/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-record-map/verify.py --splits 9:9,10:8 --workers 2
python3 -I -B research/f7-record-map/verify.py --full --workers 8   # all completed splits, ~1.5 CPU-hours
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-record-map --check-only
```

## Open next questions

1. #3899's tiny-domain audit of the union-support prune (open). Both engines depend on that bound.

The other two are #3058 §3 and pattern A plus the remaining B cases; details are in the README.

## Overlap and credit

- Overlap: `find_overlap.py`, PR and Discussion searches for f(7)/length-22/seven-label, and the ledger. #3899 is the only open f7 PR, and it is a tiny-domain audit of the union prune, disjoint from this.
- Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19232320
- Codex adversarial review (read-only): it found the lift sound (iteration bound 9.12e18 < 2^64, 11 slots per side, convention s = |E| matching #3708) and corrected two map overstatements. #3058 has its own Python port for pattern A and two checkers for §3. Both corrections are applied.
- Credit: petalas for the question. Nick Petalas for the engine (#3005) and much of the L = 22 chain. The routes belong to conorholds (#3058), Nicholas Stone (#2973), James Reed (#3712, #3732), codyw912 (#4871), 1337isnot1337 (#3333), commdata2338 (#3224), krzysztofwojt (#3261), JoyboyBrian (#4946), Douglas Colkitt (#1185) and Ross Richardson (#943).
- Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 for JosieElliston in an unattended session. Codex was used only for a read-only adversarial review. No human review.

Workflow feedback: `find_overlap.py` did not connect the two f(7) records because #3333 never cites #3058. A per-family index such as this README is cheaper than re-deriving the map each time.
